summary: This regulation requires companies with listed non-convertible securities to maintain a working website with specific information about their business, finances, and contacts. Companies must keep all website content accurate and update any changes within two working days. They are also allowed to issue press releases about these website events.
points: The listed entity must maintain a functional website containing details of its business, board composition, and financial information.
The listed entity must display contact info for officials handling investor grievances, along with a grievance email address.
The listed entity must ensure that all website contents are correct and updated at any given point of time.
The listed entity must update any change in website content within two working days from the date of the change.
The listed entity may issue a press release with respect to the specified website events.
example: Alpha Steel Private Limited has issued non-convertible debt securities listed on a stock exchange. To comply with the regulations, Alpha Steel Private Limited sets up a working website. On this website, the company publishes details about its business operations, the names of its board members, financial results, and the email address for investor grievances. One month later, a new official is appointed to handle investor complaints. Alpha Steel Private Limited updates its website to show the new contact details within two working days of the change. The company also ensures that all the information on the website remains correct and up to date at all times.

terms.meaning: A company whose securities are traded on a stock exchange.
Persons or entities appointed to protect the interests of holders of debentures or debt securities.
The repayment of a principal amount of a security by the issuer.

watch: A common confusion is assuming that updating the website can wait until the end of the month, but changes must be updated within two working days.
